name: CAP1206-1-AIA-TR
title: 6-channel capacitive touch sensor controller, SMBus / I2C
summary: The CAP1206 reads six capacitive touch pads and reports touches over SMBus or I2C, with an open-drain ALERT# interrupt. Each input calibrates itself against its pad's parasitic capacitance and keeps tracking slow drift; thresholds are per input. It adds multiple-touch blocking, pattern detection, a hold-to-activate power button, press-and-hold repeat, and RF and low-frequency noise rejection. Runs from 3.0 V to 5.5 V, with Active, Standby and a 5 µA Deep Sleep state; DFN-10 or SOIC-14, two bus addresses.
key_figures: 120 µA typ default; 50 µA typ at 1 avg, 140 ms

circuits.title: System diagram
circuits.description: Six touch pads, one on each CS input, with the chip reporting to a host controller over the two-wire bus. SMCLK, SMDATA and the ALERT# interrupt line each have a 10 kΩ pull-up to a 3.0 V to 5.5 V rail. VDD takes 3.0 V to 5.5 V and is decoupled to ground by 0.1 µF and 1.0 µF in parallel; GND goes to ground.

where.CLOAD: capacitance on one bus line, pF (400 pF max)

operation.text: Six capacitive inputs are scanned in turn and each reading is compared with a stored untouched reference (the base count). A difference beyond the input's threshold is a touch. The host either polls the status registers or waits for ALERT#. Each input is calibrated against its own parasitic capacitance and the reference keeps tracking slow drift.

Talks SMBus 2.0 or I2C, up to 400 kHz and down to 10 kHz. The -1 parts answer at 0101_000 and the -2 parts at 0101_001, followed by the read/write bit. Data go MSB first. The chip accepts a stretched clock from the host but never stretches it itself. A stop condition resets its bus interface. Only I2C-style block transfers are supported: no SMBus byte-count byte, no Alert Response Address.
Off by default. With TIMEOUT (20h bit 7) set, the interface resets if SMCLK is held low for more than 30 ms, or if both lines sit high for more than 200 µs.

Write Byte: address+W, register, data. Read Byte: address+W, register, repeated start, address+R, one data byte with NACK. Send Byte sets the register pointer only; Receive Byte reads from the current pointer, useful for re-reading one register. Neither Send nor Receive Byte works while DSLEEP is set. Block Read and Block Write move any number of bytes; the pointer steps after each byte and wraps from FFh to 00h. In a block read the host ACKs each byte except the last.

Active: the inputs enabled in 21h are scanned with the Active settings. Standby (STBY = 1): only inputs set in 40h are scanned, with the Standby averaging, sensitivity and threshold; the bus works normally and interrupts still occur. Deep Sleep (DSLEEP = 1): nothing is scanned, about 5 µA; bus traffic to the chip wakes it for the transfer but DSLEEP stays set, so it sleeps again afterwards. Clearing the bit returns to Active. A state change clears touches on inputs being switched off and resets their status.

Power-on reset holds the chip until VDD passes VPORR, then the power-up timer (tPWRT) runs before release. Brown-out reset acts when VDD stays below VBOR for longer than tBORDC; on recovery above VPORR the power-up timer runs again. At reset every register returns to its default.

Except in Deep Sleep the chip scans continuously, CS1 first through CS6, each enabled input taking its full set of averaged samples before the next. If the scan finishes before the programmed cycle time the chip idles in a low-power state for the rest of the cycle (unless BLK_PWR_CTRL is set); if it cannot finish in time, the cycle simply grows. The averaging setting wins over the cycle time setting.

Calibration tunes the analog front end to the untouched pad and then samples it to set the base count, leaving delta at zero. It runs after power-on reset, whenever the sample time changes, whenever an input becomes newly enabled, and when the host sets a bit in 26h (the bit clears itself on success). For up to 200 ms during it the input detects no touch and its base count is not valid; touching the pad meanwhile spoils the result. Analog calibration fails if a noise flag is set or the calibration value hits its minimum or maximum; the 26h bit stays set and ACAL_FAIL is raised. If the base count lands more than 12.5 % from the ideal value for the sample time, BC_OUTx and BC_OUT are set; by default the analog calibration is retried, or with BC_OUT_RECAL cleared the off-range count is used.

The base count is refreshed periodically from an average of recent readings (64 by default, set by CAL_CFG) while the delta is under the touch threshold; it stops while a touch is detected. If a recalibration moves the base count more than 12.5 % from ideal, a full calibration follows.

A run of negative delta readings (8, 16 or 32 in a row, set by NEG_DELTA_CNT; 16 by default) forces a recalibration. This recovers from a reference that was taken while the pad was touched or from drift. Touches are ignored while it runs.

With MAX_DUR_EN set, a touch held longer than MAX_DUR (560 ms to 11.2 s) forces a recalibration, clearing a stuck button. On the power button the MAX_DUR time is added on top of the hold time it needs.

One input (PWR_BTN) can be named the power button. It interrupts only after being held for a set time, chosen separately for Active and Standby (280 ms to 2.24 s), and each state has its own enable. The input must be enabled in that state. On success PWR is set and an interrupt is raised; repeat rate does not apply.

With MULT_BLK_EN set (default) only the first B_MULT_T touches (1 to 4, in scan order CS1 to CS6) are reported and further ones are blocked and MULT is set, until a reported pad is released. MULT does not interrupt.

The MTP detector uses a lower threshold, 12.5 %, 25 %, 37.5 % or 100 % of the touch threshold. In pattern mode (COMP_PTRN = 1) it fires when every input marked in 2Dh is over that threshold or flagged noisy; in count mode it fires when at least as many inputs as there are bits set in 2Dh meet the condition. An event sets MTP, blocks all touches while the condition lasts, and interrupts if MTP_ALERT is set. MTP clears only when INT is written to 0 after the condition is gone. Used for lid closure and similar.

Every input carries two noise detectors, one for low-frequency and one for RF interference; by default a sample either detector flags is thrown away (DIS_ANA_NOISE, DIS_RF_NOISE). The noise status bits show both kinds, or only RF with SHOW_RF_NOISE set. A flagged input reads delta 00h and cannot register a touch; the flags are not latched. A digital noise threshold (25 % to 62.5 % of the touch threshold) can also be enabled by clearing DIS_DIG_NOISE: a delta between it and the touch threshold is treated as a spike and kept out of recalibration.

An interrupt sets INT (00h bit 0) and pulls ALERT# low. The host writes INT to 0 to release ALERT#; status bits then clear if their cause has gone. A touch interrupts on detection and, unless INT_REL_n is set, again on release. With repeat enabled, a touch held longer than M_PRESS is a press-and-hold and interrupts again every RPT_RATE; a shorter one is a plain touch. The host may need two reads to see a release. Calibration failures interrupt only with ACAL_FAIL_INT or BC_OUT_INT set.
STBY selects Standby. DSLEEP selects Deep Sleep, clears all status and INT, and overrides STBY. INT is the interrupt flag; a touch on an input without interrupts enabled does not set it.

02h: BC_OUT (some enabled input's base count out of range, held until all are in range), ACAL_FAIL (held until all enabled inputs calibrate), PWR, MULT, MTP, and TOUCH (any 03h bit set). 03h holds one touch bit per input; bits clear when INT is cleared and the touch has ended, and a touch still present keeps its bit without re-interrupting. Entering Deep Sleep clears all of them.

Signed two's complement difference between the latest reading and the base count, updated once per input per cycle, limited to 7Fh and 80h. A reading stuck at 7Fh means the sensitivity is set too high.

DELTA_SENSE (Active) and STBY_SENSE (Standby) scale the delta count, from 128x (most sensitive, lightest touch, most prone to noise) to 1x. BASE_SHIFT only scales how the base count registers read (1x to 256x) and does not change detection. At 128x the delta MSB is 64 of about 25,000 counts, roughly 0.25 % of the base capacitance (25 fF on a 10 pF pad); at 1x it is 8192 counts, roughly 33 % (3.33 pF on 10 pF).

20h: TIMEOUT, DIS_DIG_NOISE (1 = digital noise threshold off, default), DIS_ANA_NOISE (1 = low-frequency noise does not block touches), MAX_DUR_EN. 44h: BC_OUT_RECAL (1, the default, redoes the analog calibration of an input whose base count lands off range), BLK_PWR_CTRL (1 = no low-power wait between scan end and cycle end), BC_OUT_INT, SHOW_RF_NOISE, DIS_RF_NOISE (1 = RF noise does not block touches), ACAL_FAIL_INT, INT_REL_n (1 = no interrupt on release).
One bit per input in each: 21h scans the input in Active (all on by default), 27h lets it drive ALERT# (all on), 28h turns on auto-repeat (all on), 40h scans it in Standby (all off).

22h holds MAX_DUR (560 ms to 11.2 s) and RPT_RATE (35 ms steps, 35 to 560 ms); 23h holds M_PRESS (35 ms steps). 24h sets Active averaging (1 to 128 samples), sample time (320 µs to 2.56 ms, which sets the base count size) and cycle time (35 to 140 ms). 41h sets the same for Standby, plus AVG_SUM: 1 sums the samples instead of averaging them, which can overflow the delta count on a touch.

Writing 1 to a 26h bit calibrates that input; the chip also sets these bits itself when an input becomes enabled. A bit still set while ACAL_FAIL is set marks a failed input; check only after ACAL_FAIL and after time for a fresh calibration to finish. Writing 0 over a pending 1 can skip that calibration. 2Eh shows which inputs are out of base count range. B1h to BAh hold each input's 10-bit calibration value, the capacitance balanced against the pad; 000h and 3FFh mean analog calibration failed.

BUT_LD_TH (default 1): a write to the CS1 threshold copies to all six thresholds, which can still be written one by one afterwards. NO_CLR_INTD and NO_CLR_NEG choose whether a noise flag clears the accumulated recalibration data and the negative-delta counter; set both alike. NEG_DELTA_CNT and CAL_CFG as decoded.

Seven-bit delta thresholds, one per input for Active (30h to 35h) and one shared by all Standby inputs (43h); all default to 40h. 38h sets the digital noise threshold as a percentage of the touch threshold.

The untouched reference for each input, refreshed by calibration and recalibration. Readings are summed until the sample count is reached and the top 16 bits become the base count; the register shows it scaled by BASE_SHIFT.
60h selects the input (CS1 to CS6). 61h: STBY_PWR_EN and STBY_PWR_TIME for Standby, PWR_EN and PWR_TIME for Active.

Power: supply or ground. DI: digital input, 5 V tolerant. AIO: analog input/output. DIOD: digital input with open-drain output, needs a pull-up, 5 V tolerant. OD: open-drain output, needs a pull-up, 5 V tolerant. Every digital pin tolerates 5 V.

Same pins and registers as the CAP1106 apart from the removed GAIN[1:0] (proximity gain) and ALT_POL (ALERT polarity) bits. Added: power button, ACAL_FAIL and BC_OUT flags with their interrupt and retry controls, register 2Eh flagging off-range base counts, 5 V supply operation, and -40 °C to 125 °C operating range in place of 0 °C to 85 °C.
The DFN dissipation and θJA figures assume a 1.6 × 2.3 mm land under the exposed pad with six 0.3 mm vias (2 × 3, 0.9 mm pitch) into the ground plane.
